questions.questionText: She sings ____.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: beautifully.

questions.questionText: He is a ____ driver.
questions.explanation: A noun is modified by an adjective: careful driver.

questions.questionText: The soup tastes ____.
questions.explanation: After a linking verb such as 'taste', an adjective is used.

questions.questionText: She looked ____ at the stranger.
questions.explanation: 'Looked at' describes an action, so an adverb is needed.

questions.questionText: She felt ____ after the long journey.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb 'felt', an adjective describing the subject is used.

questions.questionText: He is the ____ of the three brothers.
questions.explanation: For more than two, the superlative 'tallest' is used.

questions.questionText: Of the two sisters, Meena is the ____.
questions.explanation: Between two persons of a family the comparative 'elder' is used; the superlative forms are for three or more.

questions.questionText: This book is ____ than that one.
questions.explanation: 'Good' has the irregular comparative 'better'.

questions.questionText: He has ____ money left in his wallet.
questions.explanation: 'Money' is uncountable, so 'little' (hardly any) fits the negative sense.

questions.questionText: I have ____ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
questions.explanation: 'Few' has a negative sense (hardly any) and fits with 'lonely'.
questions.shortcut: few = almost none; a few = some.

questions.questionText: She has ____ friends in Chennai who will help her.
questions.explanation: 'A few' has a positive sense (some) and fits with 'help her'.

questions.questionText: He is ____ intelligent than his brother.
questions.explanation: The comparative of a long adjective uses 'more'.

questions.questionText: She is the ____ girl in the class.
questions.explanation: For a long adjective, the superlative is formed with 'most'.

questions.questionText: He worked ____ than anyone else in the office.
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is both adjective and adverb; its comparative is 'harder'.

questions.questionText: He ran ____ to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is an adverb without -ly.

questions.questionText: She arrived ____ for the interview and was rejected.
questions.explanation: 'Late' (adverb) means after the expected time; 'lately' means recently.
questions.shortcut: late = not on time; lately = recently.

questions.questionText: She ____ ever misses a class.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ever' means almost never; the adverb 'hardly' is used.

questions.questionText: The ____ of the two proposals was accepted.
questions.explanation: 'Latter' refers to the second of two; 'last' is final of many.

questions.questionText: The ____ news about the accident shocked everyone.
questions.explanation: 'Latest' means most recent.

questions.questionText: He gave me ____ information about the course.
questions.explanation: 'Further' means additional; 'farther' refers to physical distance.

questions.questionText: He shows ____ interest in cricket than in football.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is uncountable, so the comparative 'less' is used.

questions.questionText: She is as ____ as her mother.
questions.explanation: In 'as ... as', the adjective is in the positive form: tall.

questions.questionText: This is ____ interesting book that I have ever read.
questions.explanation: A superlative takes 'the' before 'most'.

questions.questionText: The Ganga is the ____ river in India.
questions.explanation: Among many rivers, the superlative 'longest' is used.

questions.questionText: Mohan is ____ boy in the class.
questions.explanation: A superlative with 'in the class' is formed with 'the'.

questions.questionText: She speaks English very ____.
questions.explanation: 'Speaks' needs an adverb: fluently.

questions.questionText: He is a ____ boy.
questions.explanation: A compound adjective before a noun is hyphenated: well-behaved.

questions.questionText: There is ____ milk in the fridge.
questions.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so 'some' is used.

questions.questionText: We could see ____ people at the stadium than the previous year.
questions.explanation: 'People' is countable, so 'fewer' is used.

questions.questionText: She spends ____ time on social media than before.
questions.explanation: 'Time' is uncountable, so 'less' is used.

questions.questionText: Your answer is ____ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Absolute' is already complete and takes no degrees; the adverb 'absolutely' fits.

questions.questionText: Which of the two routes is ____?
questions.explanation: Two items compared: use the comparative.

questions.questionText: This is the ____ of the two plans.
questions.explanation: With two options, the comparative 'better' is used.
